title: I’m Not Even Half by Layla Khoshnoudi at The Bushwick Starr #imnoteve...
transcript: I'm Not Even Half by Layla Khoshnoudi is a fever dream of introspection and sobering realizations. Getting hit by a car and the series of events that follow with a friend and a situationship are the chaotic backdrop to the character “S” processing the viral brutalization of women in Iran for protesting compulsory hijab laws. As an Iranian-American woman, she feels empathetic and emboldened by their courage, yet distant and somewhat guilty in her own life of comfort and safety. Through a comically train-of-thought delivery, she illustrates this type of dissonance on a smaller scale by contrasting her reactions and behaviors with those of her friend Julianne. What emerges is a deeply relatable self-awareness that makes it hard to convince herself that she's embodying what she aspires toward. Ultimately, she doesn't sort out all of her lingering questions around faith, guilt, and shame, but she does reach a breakthrough, and hopefully the audience does too. I'm Not Even Half is running at the Bushwick Starr through Halloween.
